deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a printed membership card, filled in by hand: 'No. 25. KARTE für Herrn Stud. math. Riemann als ausserordentliches Mitglied des literarischen Museums in dem Halbjahre von Ostern 1851 bis Michaelis. Göttingen, den 26ten April 1851. Im Namen des Vorstandes des literarischen Museums [signed] E. v. Leutsch.' At the foot is a printed notice: on receiving this card, the attendant (Aufwärter) of the literarisches Museum is paid 'Drei' (handwritten in a hatched box) Thaler Preussisch Courant.

The card admits Riemann, described as a student of mathematics, as an extraordinary member of the Göttingen 'literarisches Museum' for the summer half-year 1851. The term runs from Easter to Michaelmas (29 September). The literarisches Museum was a reading society and reading room in Göttingen that held journals and newspapers. The signatory is very probably the classical philologist Ernst Ludwig von Leutsch (1808–1887), professor at Göttingen, who acted for the society's board.

The date places the card in the period when Riemann was preparing his doctoral dissertation on the foundations of complex function theory, submitted in November 1851. The card is biographical evidence of his access to a periodical reading room in that semester. The pencil '47' at the right margin is the archival folio number. The previous page (a note citing Lamé's Leçons sur la théorie mathématique de l'élasticité des corps solides, 1852) has no content connection to this card; the two simply sit together in the 'Varia' bundle.

results.what: Membership card of the Göttingen 'literarisches Museum' (reading society) issued to Riemann as an extraordinary member, summer semester 1851 (Easter–Michaelmas), fee 3 Thaler Prussian Courant.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a non-mathematical administrative document, a reading-society membership card. It is of minor biographical interest only: it shows Riemann in Göttingen as stud. math. in summer 1851 with access to a periodical reading room. There is no mathematical result to evaluate.
transcription_corrections: The signature 'Ev Leutsch[?]' should read 'E. v. Leutsch', most likely Ernst Ludwig von Leutsch, the Göttingen classical philologist.
'Halb jahre': 'Halb' is handwritten into a blank before the printed 'jahre'; the intended word is 'Halbjahre'.
'Drei' is handwritten inside a hatched box before the printed 'Thaler Preuss. Cour.'.
The year '1851' after 'den 26ten April' is partly printed ('18') and completed by hand ('51'). The '1851' after 'Ostern' is handwritten.
The '47' at the right margin is the archival folio number in pencil, not part of the card's text.
No year is written after 'bis Michaelis'; the end of the term (Michaelmas 1851) is implied.
